question: Will La Jolla's tide gauge record an observed water level above 6.0 ft MLLW on October 15 or 16, 2026?

calls.reasoning: To hit 6.0 ft MLLW, the water must run about 0.89 ft above the 5.11 ft predicted high on Oct 15 (or about 1.27 ft on Oct 16). Observed highs on Oct 1-4, 2026 ran 1.02-1.06 ft above prediction, including the low-prediction days Oct 3-4, which have a similar predicted high (~5.17-5.19 ft). If that holds, Oct 15 lands around 6.1-6.2 ft. The risk is that the anomaly varies: it ranged 0.6-1.4 ft from Sep 10 to Oct 4, and was only 0.6-0.78 ft in the mid-September post-spring-tide phase, though the level has since risen about 0.3 ft. A 10-day drop of about 0.15 ft would mean NO. No matching human market found; the Polymarket peak-level contracts (7.7-8.3 ft, through Apr 2027) are near-misses with thin volume, so I did not use them.
